Formulation
Predisposing: Personal and maternal history of anxiety.

Perpetuating: Ongoing work demands, reduced sleep, possible inadequate stress-management strategies.  
Protective: Supportive partner, regular exercise, motivation for treatment, no current suicidality.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Feel calmer and less overwhelmed at work  
  • Prevent escalation of anxiety and headaches
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Reduce anxiety symptoms (GAD) to baseline/stable levels  
  • Maintain adherence to Sertraline; monitor efficacy and side effects
- Actions (Patient):
  • Continue Sertraline as prescribed  
  • Self-refer to local counseling service (link provided)  
  • Implement sleep hygiene: aim for 7–8 hrs/night  
  • Hydrate 1.5–2 L water daily; limit caffeine
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide counseling/IAPT self-referral details  
  • Review Sertraline effectiveness and tolerability at follow-up  
  • Offer fit note/self-certification advice for short work break  
  • Schedule review in 1 week; arrange blood tests if headaches persist

Secondary Problem: Work-related stress and associated headaches
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Manage workload without excessive stress  
  • Decrease frequency/severity of headaches
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Identify and modify stressors; prevent headache escalation
- Actions (Patient):
  • Consider short leave to recover  
  • Practice relaxation techniques (deep breathing, scheduled breaks)  
  • Use Ibuprofen (per advice) for acute headaches; continue Paracetamol if needed; monitor response
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Educate on tension vs. migraine symptoms and red flags (information link supplied)  
  • Reassess headache pattern at follow-up; escalate care if red-flag symptoms emerge

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Headache red flags, hydration, sleep hygiene, stress-reduction, medication use
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistent or worsening headaches, increased anxiety, sleep disruption, new self-harm thoughts
- Coping Strategies: Regular exercise, relaxation techniques, structured work schedule, counseling engagement, adequate rest and hydration
